Neovim tips from my setup: flash, smart splits and sending code to a REPL

The problem it solves

Most of editing is not typing, it is moving: to the function above, to the argument at the end of the line, to the variable three screens down. With arrow keys or a mouse that is slow and it takes the hands off the keyboard. Over a day it adds up to a lot of wasted seconds and broken concentration.

The general idea

Neovim is a modal editor: in normal mode every key is a command, so movement and editing become short phrases. On top of that, flash.nvim adds a jump anywhere on screen: press s, type one or two characters of the place you want, and every match gets a label. Press the label and the cursor is there. My configuration started from NvChad and grew with plugins managed by lazy.nvim.

Examples

My flash mappings:

{ "s", mode = { "n", "x", "o" }, function() require("flash").jump() end },
{ "S", mode = { "n", "x", "o" }, function() require("flash").treesitter() end },
{ "r", mode = "o", function() require("flash").remote() end },
{ "R", mode = { "o", "x" }, function() require("flash").treesitter_search() end },
  • s jumps to any visible text.
  • S selects syntax nodes (a call, an argument, a function) through treesitter.
  • r in operator-pending mode is the remote action: yank or delete something far away without moving the cursor.

Small remaps that add up:

map("n", ";", ":")            -- command mode without Shift
map("i", "jj", "<ESC>")        -- leave insert mode on the home row
map("n", "H", "^")            -- start of the line
map("n", "L", "$")            -- end of the line
map("i", "<C-s>", "<ESC>:w<CR>")  -- save from anywhere

Tips from my setup

  • One set of keys for splits and panes. With smart-splits.nvim, Ctrl-h/j/k/l moves between splits and Alt-h/j/k/l resizes them. It is aware of the terminal multiplexer, so the same keys cross from the editor into tmux panes.
  • Send code to a REPL. vim-slime sends the current line or selection to a terminal buffer, chosen by file type: uv run python for Python, R for R and duckdb for SQL. It gives me notebook-style running without leaving the editor.
  • Format, lint and test from the editor. conform.nvim and nvim-lint run ruff, one mapping formats and organises imports, another toggles pyright diagnostics when the type checker is too noisy for exploration, and neotest with nvim-dap-python runs and debugs the test under the cursor.
  • Other tools one key away. yazi, lazygit and fzf-lua open inside Neovim, quarto-nvim handles Quarto documents, and persistence.nvim restores the session when I come back to a project.
  • AI helpers stay out of the way. CodeCompanion and friends live behind a <leader>a prefix.

If you only take one thing from this list, take flash. It is the single plugin that changed how fast I move through code.
